classification.difficultyReason: Recognise intervals one, two and three standard deviations from the mean and use symmetry.

content.prompt:
The weights of packets of potato chips are normally distributed.
The mean is 200 grams and the standard deviation is 8 grams.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 4, centred figure below the stem
spec.description: Symmetric normal curve, a horizontal axis with arrows at both ends, seven equally spaced unlabelled ticks and dashed vertical guides to the curve. Guides use ordinary black; the curve uses house orange.
spec.mathematics: The centre represents 200 grams. Consecutive ticks differ by one standard deviation, 8 grams, spanning 176 to 224 grams.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied figure; numerical tick labels remain absent.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What percentage of packets have a weight between 184 grams and 216 grams?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}184&=200-2\times8\\216&=200+2\times8\end{aligned}$$
The interval is within two standard deviations of the mean, so approximately $95\%$ of packets lie in it.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What percentage of packets have a weight between 192 grams and 208 grams?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}192&=200-8\\208&=200+8\end{aligned}$$
The interval is within one standard deviation of the mean, so approximately $68\%$ of packets lie in it.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What percentage of packets have a weight between 176 grams and 224 grams?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}176&=200-3\times8\\224&=200+3\times8\end{aligned}$$
The interval is within three standard deviations of the mean, so approximately $99.7\%$ of packets lie in it.

children.label: d
children.prompt: What percentage of packets have a weight greater than 200 grams?

answer.worked: The normal distribution is symmetric about its mean of 200 grams. Half the packets therefore weigh more than 200 grams: $50\%$.
